newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON HOPING 6-3 DEFEAT WILL PROVIDE HAPPY OMEN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON HOPING 6-3 DEFEAT WILL PROVIDE HAPPY OMEN.

text.p: If Manchester United manager Alex Ferguson believes in omens he will be hoping that Saturday's 6-3 defeat at Southampton is a portent for his side lifting the European Cup this season.
For the last time United lost a league match 6-3 they finished the season as European champions for the only time.

Before Saturday, their last 6-3 defeat was at West Bromwich Albion on April 29, 1968 -- and exactly a month later they beat Benfica at Wembley to become the first English club to be crowned European champions.

Indeed, in their next league game after being crushed at the Hawthorns, Matt Busby's men bounced back with a 6-0 victory of their own at Old Trafford -- over Newcastle, the club which beat them 5-0 eight days ago.
Ferguson's men continue their crusade in the European Champions' League at home to Turkish side Fenerbahce on Wednesday on the back of their two worst consecutive league defeats since November 1936.
Following that 5-0 loss at Newcastle and Saturday's defeat at The Dell, statisticians had to go back into the archives 60 years to find the last time a United defence showed such frailties.
On November 14, 1936, they lost 6-2 at Grimsby in the old first division and a week later were beaten 5-2 at home by Liverpool.
While Ferguson may take some comfort from the events of 1968, he will not be looking for an omen from 1936 for at the end of that season United finished second-to-last and were relegated.
